solution: given: work \(= \alpha \cdot \beta^{2} \cdot e^{- \frac{x^{2}}{\alpha \cdot k.T}}\) \(k =\) boltzmann constant \(T =\) temperature \(x =\) displacement we know that, \(\frac{x^{2}}{\alpha.k.T} =\) dimensionless \[\left\lbrack \frac{x^{2}}{\alpha \cdot k \cdot T} \right\rbrack = \left\lbrack M^{0}{\text{ }L}^{0}{\text{ }T}^{0} \right\rbrack\] \[\lbrack\alpha\rbrack = \left\lbrack \frac{L^{2}}{K \cdot T} \right\rbrack\] \[\Rightarrow \lbrack K\rbrack = \left\lbrack M^{1}{\text{ }L}^{2}{\text{ }T}^{- 2}{\text{ }K}^{- 1} \right\rbrack\] \[\lbrack T\rbrack = \lbrack K\rbrack\] \[\Rightarrow \lbrack\alpha\rbrack = \left\lbrack \frac{L^{2}}{M^{1}{\text{ }L}^{2}{\text{ }T}^{- 2}{\text{ }K}^{- 1} \times K} \right\rbrack \Rightarrow \lbrack\alpha\rbrack = \left\lbrack M^{- 1}{\text{ }T}^{2} \right\rbrack\] \[\Rightarrow \omega = \alpha \cdot \beta^{2}\] \[\Rightarrow \frac{\left\lbrack M^{1}{\text{ }L}^{1}{\text{ }T}^{- 2} \right\rbrack\left\lbrack L \right\rbrack}{\left\lbrack M^{- 1}{\text{ }T}^{2} \right\rbrack} = \left\lbrack \beta^{2} \right\rbrack = \left\lbrack M^{2}{\text{ }L}^{2}{\text{ }T}^{- 4} \right\rbrack\] \[\lbrack\beta\rbrack = \left\lbrack {MLT}^{- 2} \right\rbrack\]
note: work = force x length, so the factor is [L], not [L^-1] (that gave L^0 instead of the M L^2 T^-2 the working needs)

solution: \[\begin{matrix} & \frac{\phi_{E}}{\phi_{M}} = \frac{EA}{BA} = \frac{E}{B} \\ & B = \frac{MLT^{- 2}}{ATLT^{- 1}} \\ & \text{~So~}\left\lbrack \frac{E}{B} \right\rbrack = \frac{MLT^{- 3}A^{- 1}}{MT^{- 2}A^{- 1}} = LT^{- 1} \end{matrix}\] Or \[E = c \cdot \text{ }B(c = \text{~Speed of light~})\left\lbrack \frac{E}{\text{ }B} \right\rbrack = {LT}^{- 1}\]
note: B = F/(qv) = MLT^-2/(AT.LT^-1) (M/T^-2 garbled); E = F/q = MLT^-3A^-1 (T^-3 was missing)

solution: \(e_{2}\) : induced emf in secondary coil \(i_{1}\) : Current in primary coil \(M\) : Mutual inductance \[e_{2} = - M\frac{{di}_{1}}{dt}\] \[M = - \frac{e_{2}}{\frac{{di}_{1}}{dt}}\] \[\lbrack M\rbrack = \frac{\left\lbrack e_{2} \right\rbrack}{\left\lbrack \frac{{di}_{1}}{dt} \right\rbrack} = \frac{\left\lbrack \frac{W}{q} \right\rbrack}{\left\lbrack \frac{{di}_{1}}{dt} \right\rbrack} = \frac{\left\lbrack {ML}^{2}{\text{ }T}^{- 3}{\text{ }A}^{- 1} \right\rbrack}{\lbrack AT^{- 1}\rbrack}\] \[= \left\lbrack {ML}^{2}{\text{ }T}^{- 2}{\text{ }A}^{- 2} \right\rbrack\]
note: [W/q] = ML^2T^-3A^-1 and [di/dt] = AT^-1; the line gave ML^2T^-2 over AT, which is not the ratio the next line reaches

solution: For objects to float \[mg = m\omega^{2}R\] \(\omega =\) angular velocity of earth. \(R =\) Radius of earth \[\omega = \sqrt{\frac{g}{R}}\] Duration of day \(= T\) \[T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega}\] \[\Rightarrow T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{R}{g}}\] \[= 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{6400 \times 10^{3}}{10}}\] \(\Rightarrow \frac{T}{60} = 83.733\) minutes \(\simeq 84\) minutes

solution: The bulb radiates \(1.25\%\) of \(1000\ W\), that is \(12.5\ W\). Treating it as a point source, the intensity at \(2\ m\) is \[I = \frac{P}{4\pi r^{2}} = \frac{12.5}{4\pi \times 4} = 0.2487\ W/m^{2}.\] With \(I = \frac{1}{2}c\varepsilon_{0}E_{0}^{2}\), \[E_{0} = \sqrt{\frac{2I}{c\varepsilon_{0}}} = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 0.2487}{3 \times 10^{8} \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12}}} = \sqrt{187.3} = 13.69\ V/m = 136.9 \times 10^{-1}\ V/m.\] To the nearest integer, \(x = 137\).
note: printed 0.249 gives sqrt(187.6)=13.70; the working's 187.3 and 13.69 come from I = 0.2487
